findings.ref: human-copy/plugins/sdd-lite/scripts/check-risk-upgrade.ps1: capability-fragment parsing block; human-copy/plugins/sdd-lite/scripts/check-risk-upgrade.sh: embedded Python fragment validation
findings.note: The supplied fragment is not validated against its documented shape. Both implementations check only that each entry has id and eligible; they do not require a non-empty string id or boolean eligible. Values such as eligible:"false" or id:null are accepted and can silently contribute no trigger or produce a synthetic malformed trigger instead of exiting 2. PowerShell additionally wraps fragment.capabilities with @(...), so null becomes an empty array and a single object with id/eligible is accepted despite capabilities being required to be an array. This violates AC-027's fail-closed shape-invalid contract.

An explicitly supplied empty or null -CapabilityReasons value is treated as though the argument were omitted, allowing keyword-only/lite-eligible behavior. The requirements distinguish total omission from every supplied-invalid path, which must exit 2; the Bash implementation also treats an empty supplied path as invalid, so this creates a cross-runtime contract mismatch.

findings.ref: human-copy/README.md sections “What's staged” and “Human-apply command sequence”; apply-protected-files.ps1:Get-PayloadFileSet
findings.note: The committed human-copy tree is not directly applicable by its own exact-set runner: README.md and .github/workflows/test.yml are recursively counted as undeclared payload. The README therefore instructs the human to copy the workflow separately and delete both paths before invoking the runner. This contradicts AC-010/AC-031's staged four-target exact-set contract and tasks.md's statement that the runner applies the staged workflow candidate with the payload; the implementation is not application-ready without modifying the staged package first.
